### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fce7cd4c46dbe7eacbf8fe108bf8ecc41e76a52c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e4f237db9f9db98893ad49f8c88d64ee6a6f3334` — the merge of head `db9b3950e94e8985c0c6030c13839149f9e68593` into base `fce7cd4c46dbe7eacbf8fe108bf8ecc41e76a52c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e4f237db9f9db98893ad49f8c88d64ee6a6f3334 && git checkout e4f237db9f9db98893ad49f8c88d64ee6a6f3334
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fce7cd4c46dbe7eacbf8fe108bf8ecc41e76a52c db9b3950e94e8985c0c6030c13839149f9e68593 && git checkout -B drift-repro fce7cd4c46dbe7eacbf8fe108bf8ecc41e76a52c && git merge --no-ff db9b3950e94e8985c0c6030c13839149f9e68593

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fce7cd4c46dbe7eacbf8fe108bf8ecc41e76a52c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

**ACCEPT** — `domain:cli` execution seat (#6024), 2026-09-12T05:12Z, against head `db9b3950e94e8985c0c6030c13839149f9e68593`. Readings below are mine, taken on this head; ⛔ none of them is the report read back.

### Gate state

`GET /commits/db9b3950e9/check-runs` — **39 checks: 34 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 0 red, 0 pending**; `mergeable_state: clean`. The 5 skipped are the usual conditional set (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` and siblings), ⛔ not a suppressed failure.

### The one thing this seat flagged at dispatch, resolved by a reading

At dispatch the card named three call sites — `compile.ts:832`, `info.ts:43`, `validate.ts:462` — and **the diff touches none of those three files**. That was recorded as something to prove, ⛔ never to infer from "unchanged means covered". Read on this head:

```
compile.ts:832    const stats = collectMetadataStats(config);
info.ts:43        const stats = collectMetadataStats(config);
validate.ts:462   const stats = collectMetadataStats(config);
```

All three reach the one reader, at exactly the lines the card named. ⇒ a fold placed *inside* `collectMetadataStats` necessarily serves all three, and the three commands' driven readings are the behavioural half of the same fact rather than three separate hopes.

### Every counted member folds — mechanically, with a control that can fail

Function body extracted from `format.ts` on this head by brace-walk, then matched:

| reading | result |
|:--|:--|
| `\bconfig\.[A-Za-z_]+` inside the function | **1** — and it is `config.KEY` inside the ⛔ comment that forbids the pattern, ⛔ not a read |
| `\bstack\.[A-Za-z_]+` inside the function | **22 occurrences across 17 distinct members** = exactly the 17 counted members of `MetadataStats` (`fields` is computed, not counted) |
| **fabricated negative control** — plant one `count(config.objects)` back in | matcher returns **2** ⇒ it can fire, so the 1-that-is-prose is a reading |

⇒ no member was left behind. That matters more than usual here: a single missed member would be invisible in every other member's correct number.

### Union, not sum — verified at the seam's source, not only by the driven control

`stack-collections.ts`, on this head:

- `if (stack[key] !== undefined && stack[key] !== null) continue;` ⇒ **present-wins**: a key the top level carries is never concatenated with a package's copy, so an object reachable from both is counted **once**. This is the property that makes the corrected number a union; a corrected count that over-counts would be the same defect with the opposite sign.
- `if (bodies.length === 0) return stack;` and `return (folded ?? stack)` ⇒ **identity return**. The no-regression claim for every stack the platform emits today therefore holds *by construction*, not by a diff that happened to come out clean — which is why `os info` came back byte-identical and `validate`/`build` differed only in the two wall-clock lines.

⚠️ **Noted, not blocking, and not a card.** Present-wins *is* the union only under the premise the docblock names — that `composeStacks` has already flattened `packages[]` upward whenever the top level is non-empty. That premise belongs to `authoringRuleUnionStack` itself (#15006) and `os build`'s union rule run already rests on it; this PR **reuses** the seam rather than introducing it. Reuse was the right call and the docblock says why: two folds that disagree would be a worse defect than the one being removed. Challenging the premise is a different card against a different seam, and this seat is not manufacturing one from a question it has no repro for.

### `Clause-②: no` — judged, not waved through

`os info` gains a refusal it did not have: a `packages[]` repeating a package id now surfaces as a named `422` / `DUPLICATE_ARTIFACT_PACKAGE` instead of `Data: 0 Objects`. That is a real change to a published command's behaviour, so it was tested against the manual floor rather than assumed harmless:

- It **shrinks** the accept set — an input previously accepted is now refused. The mechanical boundary test puts widening on the floor side; pulling back is the other side.
- It introduces **no new public vocabulary**: the ADR-0112 envelope is already published and already emitted by `os validate` and `os compile` on this exact input, above their own summary call (measured, and they are unchanged).
- What it replaces was a **false** assertion — `Data: 0 Objects` for an artifact the command could not read — ⛔ not a true line whose meaning moved.

⇒ `no` holds. ⭐ And the change is carried in the changeset in its own paragraph, which is where a user actually meets it, rather than only in a docblock.

### Instrumentation

The probe row counts over the reader's **return value** (`collectMetadataStats(project)`, summed across `MetadataStats` minus `fields`), which is the pin file's own rule — ⛔ never over `project.<collection>`, which would be a second copy of the read it watches. The floor raise 35 → 36 arrives with a **named-row test**, so a count-only floor cannot mask a row leaving while another arrives. That is the failure mode a bare floor cannot see, and it is closed in the same PR that raises the floor.

### Two things reported rather than absorbed — both correct

1. The card's **minimal repro cannot produce the exit-1 → exit-0 flip** its own acceptance asks for: it declares no apps or plugins, so its *second* warning is true of it and `--strict` still gates. The flip is demonstrated on a conforming stack instead. That is the card being wrong about its own example, said out loud instead of quietly satisfied.
2. `os info`'s refusal surface, above.

Neither was folded into the diff as a silent fix. ⭐ And #17790 was filed for the genuinely separate defect found while measuring (`os info --json` reporting `stats.objects: 1` beside `objects: []`) rather than widened into this PR.

Proceeding to ready + merge queue.
